description: We are a passionate, multidisciplinary team entirely rooted in computer science. As tech enthusiasts, we love learning, turning ideas into reality, tackling complex challenges, and understanding how things work. We constantly push our limits to expand our knowledge.
summary: Our project is a health monitoring system for astronauts on space missions, made up of an Android app (APK) and a web platform. It continuously tracks vital signs and other health indicators, storing the data locally and also syncing it in real time when a connection is available. It addresses the challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions” by solving a key problem: because of long communication delays and the impossibility of quickly returning to Earth, important health data can be lost or overlooked before it reaches ground teams. Our solution preserves every measurement and lets teams build metrics to track health status over time, enabling more complete and realistic monitoring. It is important because it supports astronaut safety and better medical decisions during long-duration missions.
details:
Our system lets astronauts and ground teams monitor health continuously. The Android app (APK) collects vital signs and health traits and saves them locally, so no data is lost during communication delays. The web platform shows this data in real time when a connection is available and allows users to create metrics and track health status over time.

Benefits: continuous monitoring, no data loss, and a more complete and realistic view of astronaut health.

Intended impact: to support astronaut safety and faster, better-informed medical decisions on long missions, where returning to Earth is not possible.

Tools: we used Rust, JavaScript, and Java to build the app and web platform. We also used AI tools such as Gemini, Claude, and GPT to support development, problem-solving, and design.

Creativity: we combine local storage with real-time synchronization, so the system works both offline and online, a key need in space.

Factors considered: long waiting times for communication, the impossibility of returning to Earth quickly, and limited access to resources in space.
